IVX HOLDINGS — FINAL AUTONOMOUS SYSTEM GAP CLOSURE, INDEPENDENCE, DEEP QA, AND PRODUCTION ACCEPTANCE

EXECUTE NOW.

THIS IS THE LAST AUTONOMOUS-SYSTEM COMPLETION BLOCK.

DO NOT RETURN ANOTHER GENERAL REPORT.
DO NOT REDEPLOY UNCHANGED CODE AND CALL THE TASK COMPLETE.
DO NOT MARK A RUN SUCCESSFUL WITHOUT TASK-SPECIFIC EVIDENCE.
DO NOT COUNT DISCOVERY, SCHEDULING, OR QUEUING AS COMPLETED BUSINESS WORK.
DO NOT USE RORK AS A RUNTIME, GIT, DEPLOYMENT, AI, WORKER, OR FALLBACK DEPENDENCY.
DO NOT CREATE A SECOND IVX APPLICATION.

FINAL OBJECTIVE

Complete and verify the IVX autonomous system end to end so it can:

- Receive owner-authorized objectives
- Break objectives into executable tasks
- Select the correct autonomous agent
- Retrieve relevant application context
- Execute real work
- Use approved tools
- Require owner approval for protected actions
- Save permanent run records
- Generate task-specific evidence
- Recover from failures and restarts
- Prevent duplicate work
- Report honestly through IVX Owner AI
- Operate without Rork
- Run safely in production

==================================================
PHASE 1 — ESTABLISH THE TRUE CURRENT STATE
==================================================

Before making changes, return the live autonomous-system identity:

- GitHub owner
- Repository
- Branch
- GitHub HEAD
- Render service
- Render deployment ID
- Render live commit
- Production /health commit
- Autonomous worker service
- Scheduler service
- Queue implementation
- Database project
- Autonomous dashboard URL or route
- Total registered engines
- Enabled engines
- Disabled engines
- Total permanent runs
- Runs with evidence
- Runs without evidence
- Failed runs
- Blocked runs
- Waiting-for-approval runs
- Duplicate run count
- Stale run count
- Rork runtime dependency count

Required status labels:

- VERIFIED
- PARTIAL
- BLOCKED
- FAILED
- NOT IMPLEMENTED
- NOT VERIFIED

Do not infer missing values.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — COMPLETE AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURE MAPPING
==================================================

Map the real production flow:

OWNER REQUEST
↓
OWNER AUTHENTICATION
↓
IVX OWNER AI
↓
INTENT CLASSIFIER
↓
OBJECTIVE PLANNER
↓
TASK DECOMPOSER
↓
AGENT ROUTER
↓
PERMISSION CHECK
↓
OWNER APPROVAL GATE
↓
TASK QUEUE
↓
WORKER LEASE
↓
CONTEXT RETRIEVAL
↓
TOOL EXECUTION
↓
RESULT VALIDATION
↓
QA
↓
EVIDENCE LEDGER
↓
DATABASE PERSISTENCE
↓
OWNER DASHBOARD
↓
OWNER RESPONSE

For every stage provide:

- Exact service
- Exact source file
- API route
- Database table
- Input
- Output
- Failure behavior
- Retry behavior
- Timeout
- Owner approval requirement
- Rork dependency
- Current verification status

Mark every missing or simulated stage clearly.

==================================================
PHASE 3 — VERIFY EVERY AUTONOMOUS ENGINE
==================================================

Inventory every registered autonomous engine.

Expected categories may include:

- Investor discovery
- Buyer discovery
- CRM enrichment
- Capital outreach
- Marketing ideas
- Technology research
- Soft audit
- Deal analysis
- Executive report
- Design review
- Developer or app-generation engine
- QA engine
- Deployment engine
- Security engine
- Data recovery engine
- Monitoring engine

Do not invent engines that are not registered.

For each real engine return:

- Engine ID
- Engine name
- Purpose
- Trigger
- Input schema
- Output schema
- Tools used
- Database tables read
- Database tables written
- External services
- Permissions
- Owner approval requirement
- Schedule
- Timeout
- Retry policy
- Current state
- Last successful run
- Last failed run
- Evidence count
- Production value created
- Rork dependency
- Completion percentage

Required final result:

REGISTERED ENGINE COUNT:
VERIFIED ENGINE COUNT:
PARTIAL ENGINE COUNT:
BLOCKED ENGINE COUNT:
FAILED ENGINE COUNT:
RORK-DEPENDENT ENGINE COUNT:

==================================================
PHASE 4 — FIX THE AUTONOMOUS TASK STATE MACHINE
==================================================

Implement and enforce these states:

RECEIVED
VALIDATING
PLANNING
WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL
QUEUED
LEASED
RUNNING
PAUSED
RETRYING
BLOCKED
CANCELLED
FAILED
EXECUTION_COMPLETED
QA_IN_PROGRESS
QA_FAILED
READY_FOR_DEPLOYMENT
DEPLOYING
DEPLOYED
PRODUCTION_VERIFYING
VERIFIED
EXPIRED
STALE
NO_ACTION_REQUIRED

Rules:

- QUEUED is not completed.
- RUNNING is not completed.
- DEPLOYED is not verified.
- HTTP 200 is not feature verification.
- A successful run must include evidence.
- A failed run must contain an exact error and trace ID.
- A blocked run must name the exact blocker.
- A cancelled run must stop further mutations.
- A paused run must not continue execution.
- A retried run must reference its previous attempt.
- A task may become VERIFIED only after acceptance criteria pass.
- A code task with no code diff cannot become VERIFIED unless the proven root cause required no code modification.
- A discovery task cannot be reported as revenue, investor interest, or completed outreach.
- A draft cannot be reported as sent.
- A funding target cannot be reported as committed capital.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — OBJECTIVE PLANNING AND TASK DECOMPOSITION
==================================================

Implement a real planning layer.

For every owner objective, create:

- Objective ID
- Original owner request
- Business outcome
- Technical outcome
- Scope
- Exclusions
- Risk classification
- Required approvals
- Acceptance criteria
- Parent task
- Child tasks
- Dependencies
- Priority
- Estimated effort
- Assigned engine
- Execution order
- Rollback requirement
- Final verification method

The system must reject unsafe or ambiguous autonomous execution until scope is resolved.

Test planning with:

1. Fix a chat-loading defect.
2. Create an investor report.
3. Prepare outreach drafts.
4. Deploy an approved backend fix.
5. Generate a new isolated test module.
6. Recover from a failed worker.
7. Pause and resume a long-running job.
8. Cancel a task before mutation.
9. Request an action requiring owner approval.
10. Request a prohibited action without approval.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — AGENT ROUTING AND PERMISSION BOUNDARIES
==================================================

Verify the correct engine receives the correct task.

Test:

- Development task routes to developer engine.
- Security task routes to security engine.
- Investor research routes to investor engine.
- Buyer research routes to buyer engine.
- Outreach drafting routes to outreach engine.
- Deployment routes to deployment engine.
- QA routes to QA engine.
- Executive summaries route to reporting engine.

Enforce:

- No engine receives unrestricted owner permissions.
- No research agent can deploy.
- No outreach agent can send without approval.
- No reporting agent can mutate production.
- No QA agent can falsify completion.
- No deployment agent can bypass owner approval.
- No worker can access secrets unrelated to its task.
- No non-owner caller can create protected autonomous jobs.

Return an access matrix:

ENGINE
READ PERMISSIONS
WRITE PERMISSIONS
EXTERNAL TOOLS
OWNER APPROVAL
PROHIBITED ACTIONS
STATUS

==================================================
PHASE 7 — OWNER APPROVAL GATE
==================================================

Require explicit owner approval for:

- GitHub writes
- Production deployment
- Database migration
- Destructive database changes
- Secret rotation
- External outreach sending
- Financial changes
- Member deletion
- Investor deletion
- Buyer deletion
- Bulk data imports
- Public content publication
- Creation of a separate application
- Infrastructure changes
- Access revocation
- High-cost AI or cloud actions

Approval requirements:

- Single-use approval token
- Task ID binding
- Action binding
- Resource binding
- Owner identity
- Expiration
- Nonce
- Timestamp
- Immutable audit record
- Replay prevention
- Approval cannot be reused for a different task

Test:

- Correct owner approval
- Missing approval
- Expired approval
- Wrong task
- Wrong action
- Wrong owner
- Replayed approval
- Modified payload
- Approval after cancellation
- Batch approval with explicit scope

Required final value:

UNAUTHORIZED PROTECTED ACTIONS EXECUTED: 0

==================================================
PHASE 8 — QUEUE, LEASING, AND DUPLICATE PREVENTION
==================================================

Audit and fix:

- Task queue
- Worker leasing
- Lease expiration
- Heartbeats
- Idempotency keys
- Retry IDs
- Parent-child relationships
- Duplicate submissions
- Concurrent execution
- Stale-worker recovery
- Dead-letter queue

Required behavior:

- One active lease per task.
- One production mutation per idempotency key.
- Duplicate submissions return the existing task.
- A dead worker releases or expires its lease safely.
- A retried task does not repeat a completed irreversible mutation.
- Multiple workers cannot deploy the same task.
- Evidence from one run cannot be reused by another run.

Controlled tests:

- Submit the same task 10 times.
- Start two workers simultaneously.
- Kill the active worker.
- Restart the worker service.
- Force a database timeout.
- Force a tool timeout.
- Retry after partial execution.
- Retry after successful mutation but failed reporting.
- Cancel during execution.
- Pause during execution.

Required final values:

DUPLICATE EXECUTIONS: 0
DUPLICATE PRODUCTION MUTATIONS: 0
LOST TASKS: 0
ORPHANED ACTIVE LEASES: 0

==================================================
PHASE 9 — CONTEXT AND MEMORY
==================================================

Verify autonomous engines receive the correct context.

Context may include:

- Current owner request
- Relevant conversation history
- Project architecture
- Current repository and branch
- Relevant source files
- Production version
- Recent failures
- Related task history
- Database schema
- Owner restrictions
- Acceptance criteria
- Available tools
- Deployment state

Rules:

- Do not send irrelevant full conversation history.
- Do not expose unrelated secrets.
- Do not use stale repository files.
- Do not use evidence from an older task as current proof.
- Preserve task memory across restart.
- Preserve owner decisions and approvals.
- Retrieve only relevant prior failures and fixes.
- Store source references for every retrieved context item.

Test:

- Task after restart
- Task after deployment
- Task after code changed
- Task referring to a previous defect
- Task with conflicting old context
- Task with owner restrictions
- Task with no relevant context

==================================================
PHASE 10 — TOOL EXECUTION AND REAL WORK
==================================================

Verify autonomous tasks perform real work.

For every tool execution record:

- Task ID
- Run ID
- Tool
- Command or request
- Input
- Safe redactions
- Start time
- End time
- Exit code or HTTP status
- Output summary
- Files changed
- Records changed
- Error
- Retry decision
- Evidence ID

Reject success when:

- No relevant work occurred.
- Only a health check ran.
- Only unchanged code was redeployed.
- The requested feature was not tested.
- A command output was fabricated.
- The same output is reused across different task IDs.
- A file was claimed changed but no diff exists.
- A database mutation is claimed without a row-level audit record.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — EVIDENCE LEDGER
==================================================

Every successful autonomous run must create permanent evidence.

Required evidence types:

- Source files inspected
- Source files changed
- Code diff
- Database queries
- Database mutations
- Test results
- Screenshots
- Device QA
- Logs
- HTTP requests
- Commit SHA
- Deployment ID
- Production verification
- Approval record
- Rollback reference

Store:

- evidence_id
- task_id
- run_id
- evidence_type
- source
- content_hash
- storage_location
- created_at
- created_by
- commit_sha
- deployment_id
- trace_id
- validity_status
- expiration, if applicable

Rules:

- Evidence must be generated after the task starts.
- Evidence must belong to the same task.
- Evidence must be immutable.
- Evidence must not contain secrets.
- Evidence must be independently retrievable.
- A successful run without required evidence must be downgraded to NOT VERIFIED.

Required final value:

SUCCESSFUL RUNS WITHOUT REQUIRED EVIDENCE: 0

==================================================
PHASE 12 — HONEST COMPLETION VALIDATOR
==================================================

Before IVX reports completion, compare:

- Owner request
- Task type
- Acceptance criteria
- Actions performed
- Files changed
- Records changed
- Tests
- QA
- Deployment
- Production behavior
- Evidence
- Remaining risks

Reject VERIFIED when:

- Acceptance criteria were not tested.
- Code task has no relevant diff.
- Only /health passed.
- Only deployment passed.
- Device QA is missing when requested.
- Production commit does not contain the fix.
- Evidence is stale.
- Evidence belongs to another task.
- A required credential or service is blocked.
- A required approval is missing.
- Rork was used in the execution path.
- The result is only narrative.

Required direct-result language:

- VERIFIED
- PARTIAL
- NOT COMPLETED
- BLOCKED
- FAILED
- NO ACTION REQUIRED

==================================================
PHASE 13 — PERMANENT PERSISTENCE AND RESTART RECOVERY
==================================================

Verify persistence across:

- Backend restart
- Worker restart
- Scheduler restart
- Render redeploy
- Database reconnect
- AI-provider outage
- Network interruption

Persist:

- Objectives
- Tasks
- Child tasks
- Run state
- Lease state
- Approval state
- Progress
- Tool results
- Evidence
- Errors
- Retry history
- Final result

Run controlled restart tests:

1. Restart before execution.
2. Restart while queued.
3. Restart while leased.
4. Restart during a read-only tool call.
5. Restart during a protected mutation.
6. Restart after mutation but before evidence.
7. Restart after evidence but before response.
8. Restart after completion.
9. Restart during retry.
10. Restart while waiting for approval.

Verify:

- No task disappears.
- No mutation repeats.
- No approval is consumed twice.
- No run changes from failed to successful incorrectly.
- Dashboard state remains accurate.

==================================================
PHASE 14 — FAILURE, RETRY, AND RECOVERY
==================================================

Simulate:

- Database timeout
- Database authorization failure
- AI-provider timeout
- AI-provider invalid response
- GitHub 401
- GitHub 403
- Render deployment failure
- Supabase failure
- Missing file
- Build failure
- Test failure
- Device-QA failure
- Evidence-storage failure
- Owner-approval timeout
- Worker crash
- Scheduler crash
- Network outage
- Rate limit
- Invalid task input
- Unavailable credential

For every failure verify:

- Exact error code
- Exact failing service
- Safe error message
- Trace ID
- Retryable or non-retryable
- Retry count
- Backoff
- Owner notification
- Final state
- No false success
- No duplicate mutation

==================================================
PHASE 15 — AUTONOMOUS DASHBOARD
==================================================

The owner dashboard must display real data only.

Required dashboard fields:

- Objective
- Task ID
- Parent task
- Engine
- Status
- Priority
- Progress based on completed acceptance criteria
- Current action
- Started at
- Last heartbeat
- Next retry
- Owner approval required
- Approval status
- Files changed
- Records changed
- Evidence count
- Commit SHA
- Deployment ID
- Error
- Blocker
- Final result

Required filters:

- Engine
- Status
- Date
- Evidence present
- Approval required
- Failed
- Blocked
- Retrying
- Completed
- Rork dependency
- Production mutation

Required controls:

- View evidence
- Pause
- Resume
- Cancel
- Retry
- Approve
- Reject
- Open logs
- Open commit
- Open deployment
- Open affected records

Rules:

- Queued tasks cannot show 65% unless measurable criteria support 65%.
- Failed runs must remain visible.
- Blocked runs must not appear as completed.
- Duplicate runs must be linked and marked.
- No fake CPU, memory, progress, or task activity.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — IVX OWNER AI RESPONSE QUALITY
==================================================

Update IVX Owner AI to respond from structured execution records.

Required format:

DIRECT RESULT

WHAT WAS REQUESTED

WHAT WAS FOUND

ROOT CAUSE

WHAT WAS CHANGED

WHY THE CHANGE WORKS

TESTS PERFORMED

PRODUCTION PROOF

WHAT FAILED

WHAT REMAINS UNVERIFIED

NEXT REQUIRED OWNER ACTION

For autonomous task responses, always include:

- Task ID
- Run ID
- Engine
- Status
- Evidence count
- Commit
- Deployment
- Exact blocker
- Remaining acceptance criteria

Never say:

- Fully complete
- Verified end to end
- Enterprise-ready
- Deployed and fixed

unless the evidence supports those exact claims.

==================================================
PHASE 17 — REAL BUSINESS-DATA BOUNDARIES
==================================================

Ensure autonomous engines do not convert research into false business results.

Investor and buyer records must be classified:

- DISCOVERED
- CONTACT_VERIFIED
- OWNER_APPROVED_FOR_OUTREACH
- CONTACTED
- DELIVERED
- REPLIED
- INTERESTED
- QUALIFIED
- COMMITTED
- FUNDED
- INVALID
- DUPLICATE
- TEST
- DO_NOT_CONTACT

Rules:

- Discovered is not contacted.
- Contacted is not interested.
- Interested is not qualified.
- Qualified is not committed.
- Committed is not funded.
- Funding target is not pipeline money.
- Drafted outreach is not sent.
- Scheduled outreach is not delivered.
- SEC records do not prove active buyer intent.
- No fake financial totals.

Every dashboard total must open the exact supporting records.

==================================================
PHASE 18 — AUTONOMOUS OUTREACH SAFETY
==================================================

No autonomous outreach may send without owner-approved campaign authority.

Verify:

- Owner approval
- Recipient eligibility
- Source
- Consent or legal basis
- Do-not-contact check
- Unsubscribe check
- Duplicate prevention
- Daily limit
- Per-domain limit
- Time-zone restrictions
- Message review
- Delivery tracking
- Bounce handling
- Reply capture
- Audit record

Test:

- One approved message
- One rejected message
- One edited message
- Duplicate message attempt
- Do-not-contact recipient
- Unsubscribed recipient
- Invalid email
- Bounced email
- Reply received
- Batch approval with limits

==================================================
PHASE 19 — AUTONOMOUS DEVELOPMENT ENGINE
==================================================

Test the senior-developer engine with real controlled tasks.

Required test cases:

1. UI defect requiring code modification.
2. Backend defect.
3. Database query-performance defect.
4. Configuration-only defect.
5. QA-only request.
6. Deployment-only request.
7. Request where no change is required.
8. Request with failed tests.
9. Request with failed device QA.
10. Request requiring rollback.

Required workflow:

- Inspect
- Reproduce
- Baseline
- Root cause
- Plan
- Change
- Test
- Build
- Commit
- Approval
- Deploy
- Production verification
- Evidence
- Honest response

Do not report development completed when no development occurred.

==================================================
PHASE 20 — AUTONOMOUS APP GENERATOR
==================================================

Verify the generator can create more than a small isolated file set.

Use an isolated QA namespace, not a second production IVX application.

Generate a QA application or feature package containing:

- Navigation
- Authentication screen
- One protected route
- One database-backed module
- API route
- Validation
- Error handling
- Unit tests
- Integration test
- Android build validation
- Web build validation
- Migration plan
- Owner approval
- Deployment plan
- Rollback plan

Verify:

- No Rork dependency
- No secret in client
- No unapproved production deployment
- Real generated files
- Real tests
- Real commit
- Clean deletion or archival after QA

==================================================
PHASE 21 — RORK-INDEPENDENCE TEST
==================================================

Block all Rork endpoints during the complete autonomous QA.

Block:

- rork.com
- all Rork subdomains
- rork-direct.workers.dev
- Rork Git router
- Rork APIs
- Rork telemetry
- Rork assets
- Rork proxy endpoints
- Rork fallbacks

Then verify:

- Owner creates autonomous task
- Planner works
- Agent routing works
- Queue works
- Worker executes
- Evidence persists
- Owner approval works
- GitHub direct access works
- Render deployment works
- Dashboard works
- IVX Owner AI reports result
- Restart recovery works

Required final values:

RORK AUTONOMOUS DEPENDENCIES: 0
RORK AUTONOMOUS NETWORK CALLS: 0
RORK FALLBACK CALLS: 0
IVX AUTONOMOUS WORKS WITH RORK BLOCKED: true

==================================================
PHASE 22 — SECURITY QA
==================================================

Test:

- Owner authentication
- Owner authorization
- Non-owner task creation rejection
- Non-owner approval rejection
- Cross-tenant access
- Worker privilege escalation
- Tool permission bypass
- Approval replay
- Task payload tampering
- Evidence tampering
- Secret exposure
- Client-bundle secret exposure
- Log leakage
- Injection
- SSRF protections
- Unsafe file operations
- Unauthorized Git writes
- Unauthorized deployment
- Unauthorized database migration
- Rate limits
- Audit-log integrity

Required final values:

CRITICAL SECURITY FAILURES: 0
OWNER-APPROVAL BYPASSES: 0
SECRET EXPOSURES: 0
CROSS-TENANT FAILURES: 0

==================================================
PHASE 23 — PERFORMANCE AND SCALE QA
==================================================

Run controlled load tests at:

- 10 concurrent tasks
- 50 concurrent tasks
- 100 concurrent tasks
- 500 queued tasks
- 1,000 historical runs displayed on dashboard

Measure:

- Queue latency
- Worker start latency
- Task duration
- Database latency
- Dashboard latency
- Error rate
- Retry rate
- Duplicate rate
- Memory
- CPU
- Evidence-write latency
- Restart recovery time

Required acceptance:

- No lost tasks
- No duplicate mutations
- Dashboard remains usable
- No false progress
- No corrupted run records
- Rate limits and backpressure work
- High-cost tasks remain owner-controlled

==================================================
PHASE 24 — 100-RUN FINAL CERTIFICATION TEST
==================================================

Execute at least 100 controlled autonomous runs across multiple engines.

Include:

- Successful runs
- Failed runs
- Retried runs
- Blocked runs
- Cancelled runs
- Paused and resumed runs
- Approval-required runs
- Duplicate-submission attempts
- Restart-recovery runs
- Tool-failure runs
- Evidence-failure runs
- Read-only runs
- Production-mutation runs in a safe QA scope

Required results:

- 100 total controlled runs
- 0 lost runs
- 0 duplicate mutations
- 0 false success states
- 0 unauthorized protected actions
- 0 successful runs without required evidence
- Every failure has an exact error
- Every run survives restart as applicable
- Every dashboard record matches the database
- Every protected mutation has owner approval

==================================================
PHASE 25 — DEVICE AND INTERFACE QA
==================================================

Verify autonomous controls through:

- Android
- iOS configuration or real device where available
- Web

Test:

- Create task
- View task
- Approve
- Reject
- Pause
- Resume
- Cancel
- Retry
- Open evidence
- Open commit
- Open deployment
- Filter dashboard
- Refresh
- Restart app
- Reopen task
- Receive completion report

Verify:

- No loading loop
- No duplicate cards
- No stale status
- No hidden failure
- No keyboard obstruction
- No broken evidence link
- No Rork reference

==================================================
PHASE 26 — PRODUCTION IDENTITY AND COMMIT PARITY
==================================================

Return exactly:

GITHUB OWNER:
GITHUB REPOSITORY:
BRANCH:
GITHUB HEAD:
GIT ORIGIN:
RENDER SERVICE:
RENDER DEPLOYMENT ID:
RENDER LIVE COMMIT:
PRODUCTION /health COMMIT:
AUTONOMOUS WORKER SERVICE:
WORKER LIVE COMMIT:
SCHEDULER SERVICE:
SCHEDULER LIVE COMMIT:
SUPABASE PROJECT:
EXPO PROJECT:
API DOMAIN:
CHAT DOMAIN:
ALL REQUIRED COMMITS MATCH:
RORK GIT ROUTER PRESENT:
RORK AUTONOMOUS DEPENDENCY COUNT:
RORK AUTONOMOUS NETWORK CALL COUNT:

Required:

ALL REQUIRED COMMITS MATCH: true
RORK GIT ROUTER PRESENT: false
RORK AUTONOMOUS DEPENDENCY COUNT: 0
RORK AUTONOMOUS NETWORK CALL COUNT: 0

==================================================
PHASE 27 — FINAL ACCEPTANCE RULES
==================================================

The autonomous system may be marked VERIFIED only when:

[ ] Complete architecture map exists
[ ] Every registered engine is inventoried
[ ] Task-state machine is enforced
[ ] Objective planning works
[ ] Agent routing works
[ ] Permission boundaries pass
[ ] Owner approval cannot be bypassed
[ ] Queue leasing works
[ ] Duplicate execution is prevented
[ ] Context retrieval is current and relevant
[ ] Tool execution records real actions
[ ] Every success has evidence
[ ] Completion validator rejects unsupported claims
[ ] Persistence survives restart
[ ] Failures retry or stop correctly
[ ] Dashboard reflects database truth
[ ] IVX Owner AI reports honestly
[ ] Business records use correct classifications
[ ] Outreach requires approval
[ ] Developer engine completes real tasks
[ ] App generator passes isolated full-flow QA
[ ] Rork-independent execution passes
[ ] Security QA passes
[ ] Performance QA passes
[ ] 100 controlled runs pass acceptance
[ ] Android controls pass
[ ] iOS configuration or device QA passes
[ ] Web controls pass
[ ] GitHub, workers, Render, and /health commits match
[ ] Zero false successes
[ ] Zero successful runs without evidence
[ ] Zero unauthorized protected actions
[ ] Zero Rork autonomous dependencies

==================================================
FINAL RESPONSE FORMAT
==================================================

Return exactly:

1. DIRECT RESULT
2. CURRENT AUTONOMOUS STATE
3. AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURE MAP
4. ENGINE INVENTORY
5. TASK-STATE IMPLEMENTATION
6. OBJECTIVE PLANNING
7. AGENT ROUTING
8. PERMISSION MATRIX
9. OWNER APPROVAL QA
10. QUEUE AND LEASING QA
11. DUPLICATE-PREVENTION QA
12. CONTEXT AND MEMORY QA
13. TOOL-EXECUTION QA
14. EVIDENCE-LEDGER QA
15. COMPLETION-VALIDATOR QA
16. PERSISTENCE AND RESTART QA
17. FAILURE AND RETRY QA
18. AUTONOMOUS DASHBOARD QA
19. IVX OWNER AI RESPONSE QA
20. BUSINESS-DATA CLASSIFICATION
21. OUTREACH-SAFETY QA
22. DEVELOPER-ENGINE QA
23. APP-GENERATOR QA
24. RORK-INDEPENDENCE QA
25. SECURITY QA
26. PERFORMANCE QA
27. 100-RUN CERTIFICATION
28. ANDROID QA
29. IOS QA
30. WEB QA
31. PRODUCTION IDENTITY PROOF
32. FILES CHANGED
33. DATABASE MIGRATIONS
34. COMMITS
35. DEPLOYMENTS
36. FAILED ITEMS
37. BLOCKED ITEMS
38. UNVERIFIED ITEMS
39. FINAL ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST
40. FINAL AUTONOMOUS VERDICT

ALLOWED FINAL VERDICTS:

- VERIFIED — AUTONOMOUS SYSTEM COMPLETE AND RORK-INDEPENDENT
- PARTIAL — REMAINING GAPS LISTED
- BLOCKED — OWNER ACTION REQUIRED
- FAILED — PRODUCTION ACCEPTANCE NOT MET

Do not return VERIFIED unless every required acceptance condition has current, task-specific, independently retrievable evidence.

Do not reuse old screenshots or previous task evidence.

Do not hide failed, blocked, cancelled, or evidence-missing runs.

Do not claim that 100 tasks passed unless 100 permanent run records exist and can be reconciled with the evidence ledger.

EXECUTE THE GAPS ONE BY ONE, FIX THE ROOT CAUSES, DEPLOY THE EXACT APPROVED COMMITS, AND RETURN THE FINAL HONEST VERDICT.
